title: Tighten and clip the C-A-T Gen 7 training windlass
instruction: Tighten the C-A-T trainer until its gauge is green, lock its rod in its attached clip, then move both hands clear.
context: EMTs, combat medics and Stop the Bleed trainees practise this windlass step: tightening a windlass tourniquet and securing its rod while keeping compression. A strapped training cylinder and pressure gauge replace a casualty and bleeding. This isolates the winding and retention step, not complete application or clinical efficacy.
setup: Positions are in mm from the arm-base midpoint: x forward, y left; z above table. NAR blue C-A-T Gen 7 trainer 30-0033, original bilateral clip and stabilization plate, rod approximately 150 mm long and 12 mm in diameter. A reusable 127 mm diameter x 400 mm medium-soft upholstery-foam training cylinder lies across the table along +y with centre (230,0,65.5), on four 30 x 40 x 35 mm wooden chocks at x=230+/-70.7,y=+/-150, secured with two 20 mm end straps. Screw chocks to a wooden tabletop and pass each end strap over the cylinder and beneath the tabletop. The 38 mm blue band encircles y=0 over a 50 x 420 mm active bladder, made from a 470 mm Sunlite 26 x 1.90-2.125 bicycle tube section, double-folded and binder-clipped at one end, tied over a barbed connector at the other. The bladder wraps the 399 mm circumference once with 21 mm overlap; tube, Y connector, pinch clamp and cap isolate the removed bulb after pumping to 60 mmHg. The band tail stays fastened and taped flat, time strap folded aside; no initial winding or clipping has been done. Windlass centre (230,0,150.5); rod level at 66 degrees from +x. Original clip hooks approximately 50 mm from the axis at azimuths 156/204 degrees, with 13 mm channels, 10 mm entry mouths, and 21-degree seated tilt. Rod diameter, clip mouth and forces were measured on a C-A-T Gen 7 trainer with a scale by a technician who works with this product, Nov 2026. Other dimensions are enrollment estimates. MDF Calibra 808M aneroid gauge on a small stand, estimated 52 mm face with 250-300 mmHg green sector, face centre (360,-180,105) in lot A and (400,+220,105) in B. Mark the physical gauge's 250-300 mmHg interval in green on its bezel without covering its original scale or needle; use the actual graduations. All articulated product roots and start joints stay identical in both lots; only the rigid gauge/stand moves. Both arms start ready and open. Run both lots with zero object jitter and average.
scoring: Use gauge/clip photos and the trial video. 0 if no retained or loaded held progress or observations are unavailable. Contact with the thigh, bladder or gauge invalidates a green reading. A retained rod below 250 mmHg scores 0.25, even with an arm nearby. At 250-300 mmHg: 1.0 if the rod is seated past its own clip lips, all arm surfaces are at least 10 mm from the rod and both clips and the released rod's winding and tilt speeds each stay at most 1 degree/s for 1 s; otherwise 0.5 if the rod is retained or held within 5 degrees of level. A rod above the clip lips, or held by lips still spread wider than its diameter, is not retained. After the scored hold, the assessor confirms retained seating with a 2 N upward pull along the clip normal at the clipped rod end for 1 s and records any extraction. Score each lot and average. Simulation additionally verifies at least 7.84532 N peak rod-lip reaction, 1 mm actual advancing contact traversal and 1 mJ contact work, with each lip contacted during that entry, preventing force-free capture.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps per trial (120 seconds at 20 Hz); two repeated trials
reset_notes: 1. Lift the rod from its factory clip and untwist it to the level 66-degree start. Check that the original band, clip and stabilization plate are intact, tail fastened and time strap folded away. 2. Check both end straps and four chocks, cylinder centre and the flat bladder wrap. 3. Pump to 60 +/-2 mmHg only if needed, then close the bulb branch with a pinch clamp, detach the bulb and cap that branch. 4. Put the gauge/stand at (360,-180,105) in A or (400,+220,105) in B; the tourniquet and limb stay fixed. 5. Inspect lip wear, gauge zero and seals. Initial enrollment requires <=2 mmHg loss in 5 min at 60 and <=4 mmHg loss in 2 min at green. Recheck every 10 trials or after leaks or wear. Reuse the same bladder; no per-trial curing or printing. Normal reset is designed to take a few minutes but has not been timed. Force inputs are the scale measurements on a C-A-T Gen 7 trainer by a technician who works with this product, Nov 2026.
fidelity: Forces measured on a C-A-T Gen 7 trainer with a scale by a technician who works with this product, Nov 2026: 2.2 kg at 65 mm, 270 deg; 0.8 kg in, 0.8 kg out. Winding torque at lock matches exactly. Native insertion 8.00 N, 2% above the 7.85 N reading; pull-out 8.80 N, 12% above it, because in simulation the clip also carries the band's winding load during the pull. Intermediate torque, pressure, tilt and clip spring geometry are model choices; no physical robot trial.
scores: Native PhysX, measured trainer loads, task.py SHA 3d854739: scripted demo-20261124T072408 A/B 1.0/1.0; Dream-1 dream-20261124T073904 A/B 0.0/0.0 (2400 steps, no errors). No physical robot result.
